notes:
The whole list is on n22.jpg, which is printed page 11. n21.jpg (p. 10) has the introduction and the key to the class numerals. n23.jpg (p. 12) starts the 'Diary from the Stations'.

Headings and columns: the table is headed 'EAST OF SCOTLAND.' with subheads in small capitals: SHETLAND, ORKNEY and MAINLAND. The columns are: 'Returns in 5 years.', '1884.' (an asterisk), map number, station with county or locality, a class numeral I.–V. (sometimes followed by '(a)'), 'Feet.' (height) and keeper.
- The class numeral is the committee's own 'migration value' for the station, not a description of the light. So I put it in 'other' and left 'character' null for every row.
- '(a)' means 'Notwithstanding the favourable description of light'; that note is at the foot of the table. It appears on rows 11, 15, 17 and 18.
- The rule under the table is followed by 'NOTE.—Read in this place part of the General Remarks at the end of West Coast of Scotland.'
- Dot leaders are given roughly; their exact number of dots isn't meaningful.

Map numbers run from 4 to 29, so 26 stations. Numbers 1–3 aren't in this list. The text says schedules went to thirty stations 'on the East Coast of Scotland, Faroe, and Iceland', so 1–3 are presumably the Faroe and Iceland stations, though they aren't printed here.

The 1884 asterisks are on twelve stations: 4, 7, 8, 14, 15, 19, 20, 22, 24, 26, 27 and 28. That matches the text's 'Twelve stations ... have sent in forty-one schedules'.

Some rows have an empty returns column: 9, 11, 12, 13, 16, 18, 22, 23, 25 and 29. Two of these still carry something: Kinnaird Head (22) has the 1884 asterisk, and Tarbat Ness (18) has a keeper, R. S. Ritson.

OCR corrections from the scan:
- The OCR's split-off fragment '.(a) 175 B.S. Ritson. / 60 John McGill.' belongs to rows 18 and 19. Ritson goes with Tarbat Ness, not Noss Head, and the scan reads 'R. S.', not 'B.S.'.
- The OCR reads the Sumburgh Head height as '3808'; the scan shows 303.
- The OCR's 'Canticle' is printed 'Cantick Head'.

Spellings copied as printed: Whalsey (Whalsay), N. Ronaldshay, Girdleness, Montroseness, Inch Keith, St. Abbs Head. Places copied as printed: 'East Cromarty' for Cromarty, and 'Elgin' for Chanonry Point, which is actually on the Ross-shire side of the Moray Firth.

Keepers: the Sumburgh Head keeper's surname looks like 'Soott' on the scan, probably a broken 'c'. The footnote on p. 12 (n23.jpg) prints 'Mr. D. M. Scott'. That footnote also says Scott moved to Lamlash, Arran, after his last schedule (Sept. 15th, 1884), and that 'Mr. Youngclause from Monach Islands' succeeded him. The p. 12 diary also gives fuller names: North Unst is 'Mr. James Edgar—formerly at Butt of Lewis' (the list's 'T. Edgar.' differs), and N. Ronaldshay's schedule was sent by 'Mr. John Tulloch', who isn't named in the list. Pentland Skerries is 'Mr. J. Gilmour'.
